Synod of Dort
DORT
proper noun
From the Dutch city of Dordrecht, where the great international Reformed synod sat in the years 1618 and 1619.

See also: Synod of Dort

📖 Biblical Definition

The Synod of Dort was the great international assembly of the Reformed churches, convened at Dordrecht in the Netherlands from November 1618 to May 1619, gathering not only the Dutch divines but delegates from England, Scotland, the Palatinate, Switzerland, and the German Reformed lands. Its occasion was the rise of the Arminian party, who in the Remonstrance of 1610 had assailed the doctrines of sovereign grace. Against them the Synod set forth its Canons, which answered the five articles of the Remonstrants point for point, and which the church has since gathered under the heads of total depravity, unconditional election, definite atonement, irresistible grace, and the perseverance of the saints. These are not the inventions of men but the plain teaching of Scripture: that the Father gives a people to the Son, and all that He giveth shall come (Joh 6:37); that God hath mercy on whom He will have mercy, not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth (Rom 9:15–16); that He chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world (Eph 1:4–5); and that none shall pluck His sheep out of His hand (Joh 10:28–29). The Canons of Dort stand among the Three Forms of Unity, a faithful confession of the gospel of grace alone, and the dictionary honours them as a true and Scriptural defence of the God who saves to the uttermost.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The great international Reformed synod of 1618–19 whose Canons answered the Arminians and confessed the doctrines of sovereign grace.

SYNOD OF DORT, the international Reformed assembly at Dordrecht, 1618–19.

It was convened to answer the Arminian Remonstrants and their five articles.

Its Canons set forth the doctrines of sovereign and effectual grace.

These are gathered under five heads: depravity, election, atonement, grace, perseverance.

The Canons stand among the Three Forms of Unity of the Reformed churches.

📖 Key Scripture

Joh 6:37 — "All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out."

Rom 9:15 — "For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion."

Eph 1:4 — "According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:"

Joh 10:28 — "And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Dort confessed sovereign grace against the Arminian corruption that made salvation hang upon the will of man.

expand to see more

The corruption the Synod of Dort answered was the Arminianism of the Remonstrants, who taught that election rests upon foreseen faith, that Christ died alike for all without effectually saving any, that grace may be finally resisted, and that the believer may fall away and perish. This was a corruption of the gospel of grace, for it removed the cause of salvation from the free mercy of God and lodged it in the will and choice of man. Dort named the error and condemned it, not as a difference of emphasis but as a departure from the Scripture that makes God, not man, the author and finisher of salvation.

The dictionary honours the Canons of Dort as a true confession and warns against the perennial return of the same error in modern dress. Wherever it is taught that God chose because He foresaw faith, or that the cross only made salvation possible until man completed it by his decision, or that the regenerate may yet be lost, the Remonstrance is preached again under a new name. Against all such teaching the Canons stand, confessing that salvation is of the LORD from first to last, and that He will lose none whom the Father hath given to His Son.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Named from Dordrecht, the synod gave the Reformed churches their Canons on the doctrines of grace.

Dort — from the Dutch city of Dordrecht.

Usage

"Like the divines of Dort, the church must answer error not with compromise but with Scripture."

"Dort teaches that salvation is of the LORD from first to last, not hanging upon the will of man."

"The Canons confess a God who saves a people to the uttermost and loses none of His own."
